Params: The bonfire has already been lit, but there is still some time before the festival officially begins. The commandant walks along the shore, and an old dock soon comes into view.
This dock was built when the islanders first settled here. As ships grew larger, there was no room to expand it, so it was slowly left behind.
Back when tourism was still thriving, it was turned from a cargo dock into a stop for small yachts and sightseeing boats.
But even that peaceful vacation scene is gone now. Only a few scattered boats remain tied here.
Compared with the busy main port, this place feels especially quiet.
A familiar female Construct is working near the dock, tending to a small boat.
Hearing the commandant call out, Bianca stops what she is doing and looks up.
Bianca's long hair is tied with ribbons in an island style, falling softly over one side of her sheer cover-up. The simple blue and white outfit is brightened by warm flowers and starfish details.
Yes. Please watch your step. The seaweed on the ground is very slippery.
The commandant carefully steps around the seaweed Bianca scraped from the hull and walks over to her.
Planning to head out to sea?
Yes. I want to visit the blue holes nearby, so I borrowed this unused boat from a local fishing family.
The blue holes here used to be famous, but tectonic shifts and climate changes have made them hard to reach.
Before the island closes, I wanted to see if there is still a way inside.
There is indeed a limestone island near this one. Its terrain makes it unfit for living, but its many sea caves give the uninhabited island a character of its own, making it a popular tourist spot.
The most famous of those caves are the blue holes Bianca just mentioned.
Small fishing docks like this don't have dry docks. Traditionally, people let the boat rest on the beach at low tide so they can clean off the barnacles below the waterline.
Apart from some signs of age, this boat's hull is in good shape.
The special coating on the outside has done a good job keeping barnacles away. That saved us a lot of work.
Now we only need to clean the cabin.
The boat hasn't been here long enough for seaweed to grow inside, but a tiny little ecosystem has already formed in the cabin.
Bianca chuckles softly and scoops up a small fish with a container.
They must have come in with the tide. Commandant, would you help me return them to the sea?
With both of them working together, the cabin is soon cleaned out. After Bianca lays down a waterproof mat inside, the boat is ready.
Do you have any plans after this, Commandant?
I'd like to invite you to the blue holes with me... Would you like to come?
The commandant boards the small boat with Bianca, and the two sit facing each other.
The tide is about to ebb, and the sea is calm.
They row in perfect rhythm. The sea breeze brushes past them, and the boat leaves a silver trail across the water.
Curious sea creatures swim past the boat. A few bold seabirds even land on the bow.
Now this really feels like a vacation.
If this is meant to be a break, Commandant, I hope you can set your work aside for a while.
I heard some residents say someone helped make a lot of festival props. That was you, wasn't it?
If you need help with anything, please leave it to me.
Even on vacation, you are still in uniform.
As if... you are ready to be called back at any moment.
I am enjoying the vacation too.
You should think of rest as part of your duty too.
I've been keeping an eye on you, Commandant.
But I'll take your word for it.
That accessory around your neck is quite special.

The commandant looks down at the simple shell ornament hanging from the neck. A little girl had put it there during the afternoon mission, and with everything going on, the commandant had almost forgotten about it.
So it is byssus. The craft of weaving fabric from shellfish fibers is rare these days.
I've heard the locals still keep some of the old techniques, but there isn't enough byssus now for mass production.
Right. The village only makes small keepsakes now, like necklaces and bracelets.
A few animal calls interrupt them.
A dolphin chirps softly as it swims straight toward the boat.
Once it reaches them, it lifts itself out of the water and shows one of its pectoral fins.
Thin silver strands are wrapped tightly around its fin.
Bianca frowns and leans in for a closer look. The commandant spots the knot first and quietly points it out. Together, they loosen the line and remove it from the fin.
The deepest part has already cut into the skin.
As if it understands that it's free, the dolphin sprays a little water from its blowhole, nudges Bianca's arm with its long snout, then swims away.
Was that its way of saying thank you?
I think so. Without your help, that line would've kept hurting it.
Mm... I hope it never has to suffer like that again.
The dolphin surfaces again with something in its mouth.
It lifts its head and tries to offer the object to the boat. It's a brightly colored starfish shell.
I think this is its way of thanking you.
Then I will accept it. Thank you, buddy.
The dolphin whistles happily and swims a few quick circles around the boat. It keeps lifting its head toward them, as if asking to be petted.

The commandant reaches out first. After a brief hesitation, Bianca also touches the dolphin's smooth skin. The playful little creature splashes a bit of water, then dives back into the sea and disappears.
By now, the boat has reached the uninhabited island. According to the coordinates, the blue holes should be nearby.
But the natural conditions may have changed too much over the decades. They can't find any sea cave entrance at all, let alone the famous blue hole.
Most of the entrances were probably submerged as the sea level rose.
There must be an entrance that is still above water.
I was thinking the same thing.
But even after circling the island, they still find nothing.
Years of waves have worn down the limestone island, leaving its coast rough and uneven.
Jagged rocks block their view, and the shadows make it hard to tell whether any cave entrance is hidden there.
As much as I hate to say it, maybe we should call it a day and stop searching for the blue holes.
Being able to come out here with you is already more than enough. I don't want to take up any more of your time. Besides...
Bianca's gaze shifts to the starfish shell resting at the bow, and the commandant looks over as well.
We met such a lovely creature.
That alone has made this short trip wonderful.
The dolphin pokes its head out of the water, swims in one direction for a while, then stops and looks back at them with another call.
Is it... asking us to follow it?
The dolphin circles back, this time with a clearer sense of urgency.
Shall we follow our new friend?
They adjust their paddles, turn the boat, and follow the dolphin.
The dolphin looks back now and then, as if making sure they are still behind it.
Finally, it stops near a steep coastal cliff.
Looking closer, they can just make out a narrow entrance beneath the foaming waves.
A chain is fixed to the rock beside the entrance, almost blending into the stone.
It was probably used by visitors to pull their boats into the cave.
The entrance is too narrow. With the water level this high, we can't go in directly.
What if we lie flat in the boat?
The commandant quickly estimates the boat's height.
They row toward the entrance. The closer they get to the rock wall, the more they feel the erratic push and pull of the waves.
The cabin is narrow. If both of them are going to lie down, there can be no space between them.

The commandant moves first, pressing against the side of the boat to leave Bianca enough room. Bianca carefully gathers her hair so it will not get in the way, then lies down close beside the commandant.
We'll need to wait a bit.
We'll let the next wave carry us in.
I hope this isn't too uncomfortable for you, Commandant.
They are so close that Bianca's breath almost brushes the commandant's skin when she speaks.
In the cramped little boat, the scent of the open sea fades beneath her soft, delicate fragrance.
Bianca is still trying not to crowd the commandant, keeping her shoulders tucked in as much as she can. She only gives a soft smile and says nothing.
The commandant shifts slightly, and the byssus necklace at the neck slips into Bianca's hair. For a moment, its pale color looks as if it belongs there.
Then a wave pushes the boat toward the cave entrance. They catch the timing and grab the chain together.
Rough stone fills their view. The hull scrapes against the rock with a harsh sound that sets their teeth on edge.
Finally, they make it into the blue hole.
